Ambient-life per-frame effects — pulse bodies (variable
Sourcesrc/experiments\star-field\engine\frame\fx.ts
UX surfaceBoot surfaces: what the user sees first on each bundle.

Members

(module scope)

Live particle-sim record stashed on each tail Points node's userData[SF_USER_GAS] — updateFx reads the seeded per-grain vectors and rewrites pos/col in place each frame (the buffers are shared with the geometry's BufferAttributes, so needsUpdate is the only GPU round-trip; nothing allocates per frame). Bare test fixtures may stub any field — every access is optional-chained and the layer is simply skipped when the record is absent.

(module scope)

Quaternion-ish — the scratch shape updateFx needs for the comet billboard math (invert, multiply). Structural so the three.js mock and the real Quaternion both satisfy it.

_mat

Billboard scratch — per-grain instance matrices are composed as translate(grain) · orient(camera) · scale(size): a tail quad must always face the camera, so its local orientation is the node's inverse world quaternion times the camera's world quaternion. The objects are created lazily off s.THREE (the module arrives on the state, not as an import) and reused every frame — zero allocation in the hot loop.

solarWindAt

Solar-wind level — the shared activity signal every wind-touched system reads from s.solarWind/s.fxTime: a slow BASE+WAVE swell (the ~11-year-style activity cycle compressed to scene seconds) plus sharp storm spikes from two detuned sines raised to a high power — rare, brief, bright gusts that make auroras ignite and flares leap.

  • @param t Scene seconds.
  • @returns Activity level (0 quiet … ~1.5 storm).

updateTail

One comet-tail layer update — the grain sim for a single Points field (positions/colors rewritten in place on the shared buffers, instance matrices composed into the pooled scratch). Module-level on purpose: declaring it inside updateFx would allocate a closure every frame a comet is live; explicit params keep it monomorphic and capture-free.

  • @param pts The tail Points node carrying userData[SF_USER_GAS].
  • @param s Engine state (camera for the billboard quat, scene t).
  • @param f Comet activity factor 0..1 (tail length/width/opacity scale).
  • @param windK Solar-wind gain multiplier for the grain column.

cam

Billboard orientation — the quads face the camera in the node's local frame: local = nodeWorldQuat⁻¹ · camWorldQuat. Without a live camera/renderer (tests) the grain buffers still update — only the matrix write is skipped.

rr

Envelope — smoothstep(0, RAMP, d) ramps fresh grains in (no pop at the nucleus), (1−d)^FADE dissolves them toward the tip, dim[i] spreads per-grain brightness, windK surges the whole column on solar storms, and GAIN pushes overlapping additive grains into saturation so the cloud fuses into a column.

if

Instance matrix — the grain's quad swells downstream (SZ_BASE + SZ_GROW·d: dispersing gas expands) and carries the seeded size jitter.

updateFx

Ambient life — the small "alive" behaviors on top of the static chart: pulse bodies (variable stars, pulsars, flaring cores) breathe via a sine scale oscillation; cycle bodies (Earth's glaciation) lerp the surface tint between the neutral white and the ice-age palette.

  • @param s Engine state.

windK

Particle tails — each layer's userData.gasPts holds the seeded grain field; this loop is the emission simulation:

d = frac(phase[i] + t·rate[i]) — grain age 0→1 x = d·len — anti-sunward drift y = lat[i]·sp + sin(wobble)·amp — lateral fan + plasma turbulence z = latZ[i]·sp·ZFLAT — thin-sheet depth sp = spread·(1 + grow·d) — solar-wind dispersion fan color = rgb·smoothstep(d/RAMP)·(1−d)^FADE·dim[i]·windK

The (1−d)^FADE term makes every grain die at its own distance — the tip dissolves grain-by-grain instead of ending on a line — and vertex-color brightness doubles as alpha under additive blending, so no quad edge exists anywhere in the silhouette. len/sp scale with the periapsis factor f (sublimation ≈ solar flux), and windK couples brightness to the shared solar-wind level so storms surge the stream. ~640 grains × a handful of flops — zero allocation.

T

One lazy scratch set for the whole comet section — matrix/quat compose targets shared by every tail layer this frame.
